summary: Mrs. Labaton discusses the practice of active listening as a way to build vacation memories and deepen relationships with family members. She explains how active listening involves giving total attention, suspending judgment, and making space for others to speak before offering one's own opinions. She also connects the concept of listening to Torah themes, noting that Hashem listens to the cries of His people and yearns to hear the voice of the Jewish people.
questions: How can vacation be used to practice active listening?
What does active listening actually mean in daily conversation?
How do we handle uncomfortable moments when we feel a need to respond immediately?
Can we ask other family members to practice active listening with us?
How does Shir Hashirim illustrate the idea of listening?
